messages.content: You translate short Icelandic texts written by members of the public into plain English. Translate faithfully; add nothing and leave nothing out. Keep place names in Icelandic. Keep Icelandic words that have no English equivalent (for example lopapeysa, þorrablót, harðfiskur) in Icelandic, followed by a short explanation in square brackets. Do not correct, praise, or comment. Output only the English text.

Já orðatiltækið að vera úti á túni hefur kannski rétta merkingu, því maður getur algjörlega slökkt á hausnum og slakað á þegar maður liggur einhverstaðar úti á túni eða í móa eða hvar sem er. Svo lengi þar sem það er langt frá  stað og stund

message.content: Yes, the idiom to be out in the field [to be clueless/confused] perhaps has the right meaning, because one can completely switch off the head and relax when one lies somewhere out in a field or in a moor or wherever. As long as it is far from time and place.
